name: UWF World Championship
epitaph: Billed as held by Undertaker at the promotion's own founding (20 June 2008); by Summer Party (28 September 2008), CM Punk is the billed champion, retaining against Undertaker there. No document read records how the title passed between them. This title's own further history after Summer Party is not established -- the promotion's own Sacrifice-era champions list (February 2009) names only a single "UWF Championship" (see that title's own record), and does not separately list a "World" championship, so whether the two were unified, or the World title simply went uncaptured, is unresolved.

name: UWF Championship
epitaph: Billed as held by Jeff Hardy from Summer Party (28 September 2008), where he retained against Edge. By the Sacrifice brand's own launch (February 2009), John Cena is the billed champion instead; no surviving document records how the title passed from Hardy to Cena. Edge earned the next challenge for it by winning Sacrifice #1's own Elimination Fatal-4-Way, aided by Randy Orton's interference; that match's own result closed with Cena, Orton, Mr. Kiz and Edge in open conflict, setting up a promised BlockDown title match not captured.

name: UWF Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Vacant at the promotion's own founding (20 June 2008, there named the "World Tag Team Championship"). Billed as held by Paul London & Brian Kendrick by Summer Party (28 September 2008), where they retain against Cade & Murdoch. By the Sacrifice brand's own launch (February 2009), John Morrison & The Miz are the billed champions instead, said in-story to have won the titles at the promotion's own New Years Party (January 2009, not independently captured); no surviving document records how the titles passed from London & Kendrick to Morrison & The Miz. A separate WAR #16 (5 April 2009) dialogue line refers to a "UWF World Tag Team Championship" as a future UW Mania stake, using the founding's own older name; whether this is the same title under its original name, still tracked separately on the WAR brand, or a slip of the promotion's own writing, is not resolved by any document read.

name: UWF Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Billed as held by Jimmy Wang Yang at the promotion's own founding (20 June 2008). A Sacrifice #1 (24 February 2009) dialogue exchange between Gregory Helms and Kofi Kingston states Helms later held this title on WAR and then lost it back to Jimmy Wang Yang, but no surviving documents carries either of those matches; Jimmy Wang Yang is the billed champion entering WAR #16 (5 April 2009), where he loses the title to Shannon Moore.

name: UWF Hardcore Championship
epitaph: Billed as held by Finlay on WAR #7 (8 September 2008), where he retains in a Six-Way match. By the Sacrifice brand's own launch (February 2009), King Booker is the billed champion instead; no surviving document records how the title passed from Finlay to Booker.

name: UWF Television Championship
epitaph: Vacant at the promotion's own founding (20 June 2008) and still without a champion as of WAR #16 (5 April 2009), whose own preview text bills a Kennedy-Bourne match to determine a new champion; that match itself was not captured.

name: UWF Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: Billed as held by Rey Mysterio from at least WAR #7 (8 September 2008), where Randy Orton attacks him ahead of a title match; Mysterio retains against Orton at Summer Party in an I Quit match built on both men's own history with the late Eddie Guerrero. By the Sacrifice brand's own launch (February 2009), Randy Orton is the billed champion instead; no surviving document records how the title passed from Mysterio to Orton. Sacrifice #1 (24 February 2009) sets up an Orton-Mysterio rematch for the following week, not captured.

name: UWF X Division Championship
epitaph: A new title, restricted to wrestlers under 110 kg, announced by Sacrifice's own GM Mr. Kiz on Sacrifice #1 (24 February 2009); its own inaugural tournament's two semi-finals (Kofi Kingston over Santino Marella; Gregory Helms over Super Crazy) are documented there, but the final between Kingston and Helms was not captured. The Sacrifice brand's own later champions list names Kofi Kingston as champion, consistent with (but not independently confirming) a Kingston win in that final.

name: UWF Divas Championship
epitaph: Billed as held by Melina at the promotion's own founding (20 June 2008); still billed as her title on WAR #16 (5 April 2009), where Natalya challenges her for a match "next week", not captured. No document read records Melina ever losing this specific title, though a separately-named "UWF Women's Championship" changes hands twice in the meantime (see that title's own record) -- whether the two are the same title under two different names at different points, or genuinely two parallel women's titles, is not resolved by any document read.

name: UWF Women's Championship
epitaph: Billed as held by Michelle McCool on WAR #7 (8 September 2008), where she retains by disqualification against Candice Michelle. Beth Phoenix won the title outright from McCool's own team in an 8-Diva Tag Team Ladder match at Summer Party (28 September 2008), and is still billed champion on the Sacrifice brand's own later champions list (February 2009). A WAR #16 commentary tease (5 April 2009) separately promises "Beth Phoenix defende [o título] contra Candice Michelle", suggesting Phoenix's reign continued at least that far, though under a title name this document does not itself use.
